name: Octopus ring: Thomas pulse, +20 ms per coil, counter-clockwise (Cook 1999, Booth 2008)
origin: Persinger & Koren lab, Laurentian University (circumcerebral 'Octopus': Cook 1999, Richards 2002, Booth 2008)
summary: The circumcerebral configuration Persinger's lab reported as most effective: the frequency-modulated Thomas pulse rotated counter-clockwise around a ring of 8 coils, staying 20 ms longer on each successive coil (100, 120 ... 240 ms). The lab reported that it lengthened subjective time compared with clockwise rotation (Cook 1999), raised theta power by about 30% (Richards 2002) and raised power over the right hemisphere (Booth 2008).
notes: This follows the verified reading of the papers: the effective configuration added 20 ms at each successive solenoid (Cook 1999: "Successive additions of 20 ms of the complex fields ... at each solenoid"; Richards 2002: "20-msec. rates of change"; Booth 2008: "20 ms rates of change"), not a fixed 20-ms dwell. The base duration at the first coil is 100 ms, the only base the lab pairs with a 20-ms change: Persinger, Koren & Tsang 2003 describe the same stimulus as "presented for 100 msec. with changes in rate of 20 msec. to each of the eight solenoids", and Table 1 of the Swann paper (Persinger, Roll, Tiller, Koren & Cook 2002) prints the lab's three rotation rates as base 20 ms with +2, base 100 ms with +20 and base 200 ms with -2. So the dwell grows 100, 120 ... 240 ms, one turn 1360 ms, which sits inside Cook's "about 200 and 2000 ms" for its three rotation durations (the same table's other two turns are 216 and 1544 ms). Persinger & Lavallee 2010 instead gloss the effective condition as '20+2' (20, 18 ... 6 ms, a 104-ms turn), the reading persinger-mood-rotated-burst-2009 uses; one of the two is wrong and the abstracts do not settle it. The full six-pattern batteries of these papers are already built as persinger-cook-1999-time-ccw and -cw (Cook's six 2.5-min patterns) and persinger-booth-2008-cw-ccw (the same six each way); this program isolates the single configuration the papers call most effective. Cook 1999 ran six patterns of 2.5 min each with three rotation rates at about 10 uT, counter-clockwise in one group and clockwise in the other; Richards 2002 ran six 5-10 uT configurations; Booth 2008 compared clockwise and counter-clockwise rotation of the same patterns; none documents a 20-30-min session. This program runs the one described configuration for 5 min (stop at 2.5 min to match Cook); run persinger-octopus-plus20-cw on another day, blinded if possible, for the comparison. Approximations: the waveform is the Thomas pulse played from its exact table (849 points at 3 ms, one 2.55-s decelerating burst, repeating with no gap), because Saroka's dissertation says Cook used it; Richards and Booth do not name theirs. The Swann table pairs this rotation with a 2-ms point duration and a 1-ms gap between repeats; 3 ms is the point duration the lab's own descriptions of the Thomas file give, and the one used here, so the pattern runs half as fast as that table implies. The ring is 8 coils about 45 degrees apart on the 10% line with coil 1 over the left frontal region and coil 8 over the right prefrontal region, counter-clockwise seen from above (Persinger & Lavallee 2010): Fp1, FFT7, TP7, POO7, POO8, TP8, FFT8, Fp2, an inference since the lab gives no electrode names. The ramp starts at coil 1 in both directions, so here the right-hemisphere coils get the longer dwells (180-240 ms) and in the clockwise program the left ones do; the papers do not say how their clockwise runs were sequenced, so direction and dwell asymmetry cannot be separated. Intensity: about 10 uT (Cook) or 5-10 uT (Richards) in the originals; 5 uT, this helmet's maximum, is the default (Lehman measured 1-5 uT inside each solenoid of the lab's ring). Directions are as seen from above. Single lab, no blinding or sham arm described in the abstracts, never independently replicated; subjective time estimates are easily swayed by expectation. Independent double-blind tests of God-Helmet-type fields found no field effect (Granqvist 2005; Gendle & McGrath 2012). Not for anyone with epilepsy or a seizure history; stop on headache, nausea or distress.
setting: Seated, eyes closed, in a quiet, dim room (the lab used an acoustic chamber). For the original measures, estimate a 10-s interval afterwards or record EEG during the session.
schedule: One 5-min session (2.5 min per pattern in Cook 1999); compare with the other direction on a separate day.
source: Cook, Koren & Persinger 1999, Neurosci Lett 268:61 https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/10400078/ ; Richards, Koren & Persinger 2002, Percept Mot Skills 95:671 https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/12434867/ ; Persinger, Koren & Tsang 2003, Percept Mot Skills 97:877 (the same rotation as 100 ms with 20-ms changes per solenoid) https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/14738355/ ; Persinger, Roll, Tiller, Koren & Cook 2002, Percept Mot Skills 94:927, Table 1 (the lab's three base dwells and changes) https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/12081299/ ; Booth, Koren & Persinger 2008, Electromagn Biol Med 27:426 https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/19037792/ ; Saroka 2016, PhD dissertation, Laurentian University (Cook 1999 used the Thomas pulse on the 'Octopus') https://laurentian.scholaris.ca/server/api/core/bitstreams/be015982-0b0f-4c27-a031-797637c364e1/content ; Persinger & Lavallee 2010, J Conscious Explor Res 1(7):785 (ring order and the '20+2' notation) https://jcer.com/index.php/jcj/article/view/99 ; Lehman 2016, PhD thesis, Laurentian University, pp. 56-57 (CCW standard, 1-5 uT inside each solenoid) https://laurentian.scholaris.ca/items/e809389f-805c-4414-8177-d0bf8d7127bb ; Buckner et al. 2015, PLoS ONE 10:e0124136 (Thomas file: 849 points at 3 ms, 2.55 s) https://europepmc.org/article/MED/25875081 ; US 6,234,953 B1, Table 1 (Thomas pulse point values) https://patents.google.com/patent/US6234953B1/en ; Granqvist et al. 2005, Neurosci Lett 379:1 https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/15849873/ ; Gendle & McGrath 2012, Percept Mot Skills 114:217 https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/22582690/
